_comment: Authoritative schema for the OLCF Summit per-component power+thermal parquet files, transcribed verbatim from the dataset README DATA-SPECIFIC INFORMATION section (2026-08-10). Physical meaning cross-checked against the SC'21 companion paper. VERIFY against real parquet headers once downloaded (feasibility question C-H).
row_grain: one row per (hostname, timestamp); ALL component signals for that node are columns in the SAME wide row -> CPU/GPU temp and power are co-located by construction (no join).

timestamp.note: precision/timezone TO VERIFY on real data

hostname.note: physical rack position encoded; stability within dataset TO VERIFY

per_core.note: 23 cores per socket; core index 13 is EXCLUDED (absent by design). units=Celsius, dtype=float32 (NOT 1C-quantized).

cpu_temperature.pilot_choice: use p0_core_temp_mean and p1_core_temp_mean as the socket temperature T for the first-order model

cpu_power.note: per-socket. p0_power pairs with p0_core_temp_mean; p1_power with p1_core_temp_mean.

gpu_power.note: GPUs grouped under the socket they hang off (p0 -> gpu0/1/2, p1 -> gpu0/1/2). Map to gpuN_core_temp by verifying the naming correspondence on real data before pairing.

cooling_boundary.provenance: OLCF documentation/blog: medium-temperature direct liquid cooling, node inlet ~21C. NOT a column in the dataset.
cooling_boundary.usage: treat as a CONSTANT assumed boundary T_ref; in the first-order ARX baseline T_ref is absorbed into the intercept gamma, so a constant value is harmless but must be labeled ASSUMED, not measured. Does NOT vary in time and is NOT node-specific in this dataset.

sampling_interval_nominal_s.note: these are aggregated MEANS over the interval; raw 1Hz is NOT in the public release

v1_baseline_adapter.target: src/baseline ClassicalBaselineModel.fit(segments) where segments = list of (T_array, P_array)
v1_baseline_adapter.note: V1 model used READ-ONLY via a V2 adapter; V1 is NOT modified. Adapter only reshapes columns into (T,P) segments split on timestamp gaps.
